transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-04-20 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (CTO, Sapphire Concourse), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Carlos Ruiz (Infra Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Customer evaluating open models for long-doc summarization and tool integration. Main constraints: context length, bilingual support, audit/KMS requirements for private data, and predictable throughput for peak business hours.

00:00 Jordan Park: okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining, um quick intros — i'm Jordan, account exec at Redwood. Maya is our solutions engineer. can you do quick intros on your side?
00:12 Liam O'Neill: yeah sure, Liam O'Neill, CTO at Sapphire Concourse. we're building a docs-automation suite for logistics contracts. Priya is our ML lead and Carlos runs infra.
00:20 Priya Singh: hi all, we own model selection and productionization, we've been prototyping with a couple open models locally.
00:26 Maya Chen: awesome, glad to hear that, today we'll try to cover model choices, context lengths, multilingual needs and how tool-calling would map to your search/sql systems.
00:38 Jordan Park: and from a business lens i want to understand timeline and success metrics — when do you need to be in pilot, and what would success look like?
00:46 Liam O'Neill: timeline is tight, we'd like pilot in 3–4 weeks. success: accurate contract summarization (recall of clauses > 95% on eval set), latency under 800ms p50 for short summaries but we accept up to 3s for full doc operations, and costs should be within our budget — we'll share more.
01:05 Priya Singh: also multilingual — English and Spanish are immediate, Japanese in Q3. many docs are bilingual, so ability to keep context across languages is key.
01:16 Maya Chen: got it. quick question on context: when you say full doc operations, what's average doc length and worst case?
01:23 Priya Singh: averages around 2k tokens, but we have big bundles — some contracts + annexes hit 40k tokens; worst case we saw 68k. so we need long-context model support, ideally up to 64k and plans for >64k.
01:39 Jordan Park: ok that puts Hosted with our 8k/32k default out of the box for small tests, but we also support larger context models and specialized configurations on Dedicated/Private for 64k+. Maya?
01:50 Maya Chen: yep. technically we can run 64k or 128k context depending on model family and config. trade-offs: higher memory & cost, and throughput lower per-GPU. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput for those large contexts; Private lets you control KMS/HSM and network egress, which matters for compliance.
02:12 Carlos Ruiz: on compliance we have SOC2 and some EU residency requirements for certain customers. We need audit logs, KMS integration (can be external HSM), and VPC peering. Does Redwood Private support customer KMS?
02:25 Maya Chen: yes, Private supports customer KMS integrations and HSM via standard interfaces, and audit logs are included. There's some ops setup for HSM key provisioning. We'll share the security appendix.
02:36 Jordan Park: also note Dedicated can be isolated within our cloud account and we can do reserved pools; that's less ops heavy than on-prem Private but still gives isolation.
02:45 Liam O'Neill: good. on tool-calling: we have an internal vector DB and a SQL microservice that runs structured lookups. we'd like the model to call our fetch/search endpoints and then run a template to fill summaries. Is that supported?
02:58 Maya Chen: yes, Redwood supports tool-calling patterns and function calling. Common pattern is model issues a function call to your vector search or SQL service, we proxy or you can host the tool endpoint in your VPC. Need to talk through auth — short-lived tokens or signed requests.
03:16 Priya Singh: latency of those external calls is a concern — a single doc flow can have multiple vectors + SQL hits. Can we pipeline or cache KV to reduce calls?
03:26 Maya Chen: absolutely — we have prefix/KV caching features and batching, and you can surface top-K retrievals in a single call to minimize round trips. Also TTL caches for embedding results can help.
03:40 Jordan Park: wanted to ask about model families you are testing locally — Priya mentioned open models? which ones?
03:47 Priya Singh: we've tried a couple: Llama2 derivatives, MPT variants, and one of the new 70B open models (they call it 'Argos' internally) — accuracy varies and memory footprint is big on 70B.
03:57 Maya Chen: right — different families have different tradeoffs on latency, instruction-following, and long-context handling. we can share a model matrix that maps to cost per 1k tokens, expected p95 latency at different context sizes, and typical quality notes.
04:12 Liam O'Neill: we'd like to see Spanish performance explicitly — often benchmarks are in English only.
04:18 Maya Chen: noted, we'll include bilingual benchmarks and give guidance on fine-tuning vs prompting strategies. For Spanish, some LLMs have good base performance; others need a small domain-tuning pass.
04:30 Carlos Ruiz: for Dedicated or Private, how are rollouts handled? we need controlled rollouts and quick rollback if a model degradation happens.
04:38 Maya Chen: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B routing, and automatic fallback to a lower-latency variant if quality or latency SLOs break. You can pin model versions per route.
04:50 Jordan Park: cool. budget question — roughly what delta between Hosted standard vs Dedicated reserved for a 64k-capable setup? even ballpark numbers help.
04:58 Maya Chen: it depends on traffic profile. Ballpark — hosted for intermittent usage is cheaper short-term; Dedicated reserved (monthly commit) amortizes cost if you're doing high qps. We'll put concrete scenarios in the pilot TCO spreadsheet.
05:12 Priya Singh: pilot — we want to test 32k and 64k context runs, Spanish docs, tool-calling to vector+SQL, and a small load test simulating peak hour (~30 qps). can Redwood run the load tests as part of pilot?
05:24 Jordan Park: yes we can run coordinated benchmarks. Maya will lead the test plan.
05:28 Maya Chen: plan: 1) baseline model runs locally on your sample docs (we'll provide scripts), 2) hosted quick run for faster iteration, 3) dedicated long-context runs for 64k/128k to measure p50/p95 and cost, 4) tool-calling integration tests with your staging endpoints. We'll need sample data and endpoints.
05:47 Carlos Ruiz: note staging can't accept external credentials; we need to host tools inside the VPC. How do we set up function auth?
05:56 Maya Chen: two options: we proxy calls via Redwood Private (if you choose VPC) or we use short-lived signed tokens for Hosted/Dedicated and you accept those at the staging endpoint. For strict staging VPC-only you'll want Private mode.
06:12 Liam O'Neill: for pilot timeline, is 3–4 weeks realistic?
06:16 Jordan Park: yes if we get sample data and your infra window quickly. Week 1: dataset ingest and baseline. Week 2: bilingual tests and tool-calling. Week 3: load tests and final report. We can compress if both teams prioritize.
06:30 Priya Singh: one more — model hallucinations on legal text are a concern. we'd like to measure factuality and have regression alerts.
06:38 Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize supports quality-monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals. We'll instrument metrics for hallucination rate on your eval set and wire alerts.
06:51 Jordan Park: ok let's capture decisions: we will propose a pilot that uses Hosted for iteration, then Dedicated for 64k runs, with option to move to Private if KMS/HSM or VPC constraints require. Agreed?
06:59 Liam O'Neill: that sounds right. any blockers from infra? Carlos?
07:02 Carlos Ruiz: we need to validate legal for cross-border data flow and verify HSM compatibility. Also need to know if Redwood can provide SOC2/ISO proof for the Hosted environment because some customers push back.
07:13 Jordan Park: we'll include SOC2 docs and the security appendix. For HSM we documented integration patterns in the pack.
07:20 Priya Singh: can you also include recommended quantization strategies? we may want to try 4-bit or q4f16 to reduce memory for 70B-style models.
07:28 Maya Chen: yes, we'll include quantization recommendations and expected quality delta. note that some long-context kernels interact with quantization differently; we'll document which model variants we suggest.
07:39 Liam O'Neill: anything else — monitoring, alerting, SSO?
07:44 Jordan Park: Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC. We'll include steps for SCIM provisioning if you want automated user provisioning.
07:52 Priya Singh: perfect.
07:55 Jordan Park: wrap up — next steps recap: Jordan sends pilot + pricing + SOC2 pack by 2027-04-23; Priya uploads sample docs by 2027-04-22; Maya shares benchmark plan by 2027-04-24; schedule infra deep-dive for 2027-04-26 (Carlos + Maya).
08:16 Liam O'Neill: thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
08:20 Jordan Park: thanks all, chat offline on timing and we'll follow up with calendar invites.
